title: Roman Citizenship
lead: Roman citizenship carried protection under law. Paul used it at Philippi and Jerusalem, and Tacitus records emperors handing it out to whole peoples for political gain.

sections.b: Tacitus says the Gauls were tied to Galba by the recent gift of Roman citizenship (1:8), and that Otho gave Roman citizenship to all the Lingones (1:78). Wikipedia's page on the auxiliaries says that retiring auxiliaries and their children were awarded citizenship, and that this is deduced from the date of the first known military diplomas.
sections.refs: Histories of Tacitus 1:8; Histories of Tacitus 1:78

sections.b: Paul told the Philippian magistrates, "We are Romans" (Acts 16:37). At Jerusalem the commander said, "It cost me a great deal of money to acquire this citizenship." Paul said, "I, though, was born to it" (Acts 22:28).
